title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
problemStatement: Add k gas stations on a line to minimise the maximum distance between adjacent stations.
intuition: For a candidate distance d, the number of stations needed in a gap of length g is floor(g/d). That count is monotone in d, so binary search over real numbers with a precision bound.

approaches.title: Better: max-heap of gaps
approaches.idea: Repeatedly split the currently largest section.
approaches.code:
import heapq


def min_max_gap_heap(stations: list[int], k: int) -> float:
    heap = [(-(stations[i + 1] - stations[i]), i, 1) for i in range(len(stations) - 1)]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    for _ in range(k):
        neg, i, parts = heapq.heappop(heap)
        parts += 1
        seg = stations[i + 1] - stations[i]
        heapq.heappush(heap, (-(seg / parts), i, parts))
    return -heap[0][0]
limitations: k can be 10^9, making the loop infeasible

approaches.title: Optimal: binary search on the real answer
approaches.idea: Count required stations for a candidate d; iterate to a fixed precision.

approaches.whyWorks: needed(d) is non-increasing in d, so the feasible set is an interval.

commonMistakes: Looping while hi - lo > eps without a hard iteration cap
Integer division when the answer is fractional
patternRecognition: Real-valued answers -> fixed iteration count instead of an integer boundary
followUps: Why does the heap solution fail for large k?
interviewInsight: Using a fixed 100 iterations instead of an epsilon loop is a neat robustness trick worth stating.
